# Education in Finland
Finland’s education system emphasizes comprehensive, equitable, and high-standard learning from early childhood through tertiary levels. Early childhood education, including free universal daycare (ages 8 months to 5 years) and compulsory kindergarten at age six, focuses on play-based learning and developing social and communication skills. Primary and lower secondary education (grades 1–9) is compulsory, with free school lunches, minimal homework, small class sizes, and an emphasis on individualized growth and cooperation rather than tracking or gifted programs. Students learn multiple languages and engage in diverse subjects, including arts and crafts, fostering broad-based development.
Upper secondary education (ages 15–18) became compulsory in 2021, offering academic (lukio) and vocational tracks that both provide pathways to higher education. Teachers at all levels must hold master’s degrees, and the profession is highly respected with competitive university admissions. Finnish tertiary education is dual-structured into state-owned universities—with a strong research and theoretical focus—and universities of applied sciences offering practice-oriented education linked to workforce needs. Admissions are meritocratic and transparent, relying on matriculation exam results and entrance tests without subjective criteria. Adult education includes diverse free and low-cost courses through numerous independent institutions promoting lifelong learning and civic participation. Finnish education policy encourages phenomenon-based learning and continuous reform to maintain its globally recognized high quality and inclusiveness.
